source_context.caption_hook: Supply-chain roles are framed as different birds in one flock.
caption_argument: Each function has a recognisable operating personality.
The humour is intentionally affectionate rather than technical.
The closing prompt invites readers to name their own S&OP 'bird'.
observed_performance_context: Included in Tiger's intentionally curated Top-100 reference set.

reader_situation.primary_reader: Any supply-chain practitioner who has experienced the predictable personalities and tensions between adjacent functions.
reader_situation.work_moment: A reader is scrolling between operational problems and wants to feel seen before they want a technical lesson.
reader_situation.tension: Cross-functional friction is real, but explaining it directly can sound accusatory or tedious.
reader_situation.topic_selection_boundary: This record does not choose a topic, identity set, metaphor or future post angle.

attention_physics.thumbnail_read_0_3_seconds: The headline 'Supply Chain Roles as Birds' creates an immediate, unexpected category collision; seven colourful character portraits make the post legible even before the text is read.
attention_physics.comprehension_3_10_seconds: The stacked rows turn the reader into a self-directed quiz: role -> bird -> funny truth -> icon. The reader scans for their own role first.
attention_physics.value_exchange_10_30_seconds: The post gives a socially safe language for role differences and a small moment of workplace recognition rather than a formal framework.
attention_physics.identity_or_curiosity_trigger: 'Which one are we?' is more compelling than 'Here are seven functions.' The post uses affiliation and humour as the entry point.
attention_physics.promise_proved_by_visual: Distinctive birds, numbers and colour-coded rows show the mapping immediately; the visual has enough personality to carry the premise without the caption.

visual_forensics.asset_specific_observation: Tall seven-row identity list using large illustrated birds, role labels and one short behavioural reveal per row.
visual_forensics.composition_and_grid: Tall, evenly stacked seven-row list. Each row has a large numbered badge, an expressive bird portrait, a role label, a short character sentence, and a small reinforcing icon/line on the right.
visual_forensics.dominant_anchor: The birds—not the text—are the recognition devices. Their faces, clothes and poses assign personality before explanation.
visual_forensics.hierarchy: Role labels are bold and dominant within each row; the humour line and supporting icon work as quick second and third beats.
visual_forensics.typography: Huge condensed/sans headline, bold uppercase role labels, then a mixture of normal and handwritten/script accents for personality.
visual_forensics.colour_material_and_contrast: Warm off-white paper-like background lets the vivid birds carry colour. Each row receives a distinct accent colour, but the system stays unified through repeated card structure.
visual_forensics.imagery_role: The illustrations are semantic characters, not decoration. They give the stereotype an emotional and memorable body.
visual_forensics.density_and_pacing: Very low cognitive load per row; the reader can consume one joke at a time and continue because each row promises a new reveal.
craft_observations: The taxonomy is deliberately incomplete in a technical sense but complete in a social-recognition sense.
Rows are self-contained, which makes it highly scrollable and commentable.
Humour lowers the defensiveness that a literal role critique could trigger.

content_mechanics.primary_cognitive_job: Create benign self-recognition that makes a shared work tension socially discussable.
content_mechanics.compression_method: Archetype mapping: a dense job description becomes one memorable creature and one behavioural truth.
content_mechanics.reader_payoff: A memorable, human way to name cross-functional tendencies without claiming a universal organisational truth.
save_share_return_motives: Send to a colleague for a low-friction inside joke
Use as a prompt for a team conversation
Return for a quick role map
content_mechanics.caption_to_visual_choreography: The image executes the joke and gives all seven reveals. The caption broadens it into the shared-mission idea and asks the reader to participate with their own mapping.

mechanism_fingerprint.primary_cognitive_job: Create benign self-recognition that makes a shared work tension socially discussable.
social_action_mechanics: send as a friendly inside joke
revisit as a team conversation starter
use_when: The chosen opportunity contains a widely recognisable but low-stakes human pattern.
A metaphor can add warmth without erasing important nuance.
The desired response is recognition, participation or discussion before instruction.
do_not_use_when: The content needs technical precision, a sensitive critique or a substantiated outcome claim.
The metaphor would stereotype, humiliate or simplify a real power imbalance.
The reader requires a step-by-step action rather than social recognition.
mechanism_fingerprint.topic_selection_boundary: This mechanism chooses no group, event, metaphor or workplace issue. It only defines the conditions under which an identity mirror can work.

transferable_atoms: Use an unexpected but readable metaphor for a real work identity.
Make every row reveal one recognisable behavioural truth.
Keep criticism affectionate and specific enough to prompt tagging.
Use the caption for community participation, not for repeating the visual.
recombination.reverse_build_specification: When a selected opportunity contains a shared, low-stakes workplace identity and needs recognition before instruction, use one original metaphor to create several self-contained archetype reveals. Let the reader find themselves first, then scan the adjacent perspectives. Keep each reveal kind, specific and independently legible. Make the visual deliver the social recognition; let the caption establish the common tension and invite contribution. Require lived-language and a fairness check. Do not use where precision, sensitivity or evidence is the primary need, and do not borrow animal characters, the flock premise, wording, illustrations or typography from the source.
required_original_inputs: Language practitioners use to describe the tension
A fairness check so no role is mocked or reduced to a caricature
recombination.falsification_question: Do practitioners recognise a real moment and voluntarily tag or add a missing perspective, rather than merely liking the illustration?
